input.task: Who submitted the Aurora Desk Lamp teardown?

provenance: M38, rung 1. Deployment runs 349e4839 / e08b7627 / bcae4fe7 / 63b9d944 (HN item 1, 'Who submitted this story?'): `extract {role: link, name: "pg"}` resolved to two elements and the run died `ResolveError: 2 matches at tier role`; the relocation rung retargeted as `{text: "pg"}` and hit the same two. Four spent runs, an answer that was on the page, and a plan that named it. The page itself settles the ambiguity — one of the two links sits inside the submission subline the task is about — and the plan already carries a string from that subline: the identity anchor. Watched red first: `status failure:locate`, reason `step 3 (extract): relocation after locate failure: retargeting as {'text': 'user profile'}; ResolveError: no tier resolved {'text': 'user profile'}` — i.e. the role tier raised `ambiguous-match: 2 matches`, the ladder spent its one legitimate rung retargeting at the text tier, and that rung found nothing at all, because 'user profile' is an aria-label and no text on the page says it. Two matches, one of them right, and the run ends with no answer. T-M38-2 structured-field red: the same successful run kept `narrowed: anchor-proximity` only in note while `resolved.narrowed` was absent; the precise case returned `resolved_narrowed: false` before the trace writer was changed.

triage.what_this_grades: that the identity anchor is used as a PROXIMITY tiebreaker when a tier is ambiguous and the plan gave no `near`. The two candidates carry the same accessible name and DIFFERENT readings ('arden' vs 'bellweather'), so the case fails if the resolver picks by document order instead — this is the shape where the cheap rung is a wrong answer, and it is why rung 2 (document order) refuses matches that do not read identically.
triage.not_covered: whether the anchor is a GOOD proximity signal in general. It is opportunistic: an anchor that identifies no single place on the page, or that is nearer some other candidate, resolves nothing here and the run falls through to the next rung or fails loudly — but an anchor that is confidently near the WRONG candidate produces a confident wrong answer, which is the accepted risk recorded in ADR-026.
